newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-TROUBLED PSG RELINQUISH TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUBLED PSG RELINQUISH TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Troubled Paris St Germain, who had to share points with lowly Cannes at the weekend, said they had abandoned hope of winning the French league title and would need to fight to stay second.
"We're not thinking about the title anymore," manager Ricardo said after Saturday's 1-1 draw with Cannes at the Parc des Princes. "Now our goal is to stay second and even that will not be easy."
PSG, desperate for a home win since early November, are now seven points behind leaders Monaco, who drew 3-3 at Lyon on Sunday.
Bastia, who beat Strasbourg 3-1 at home, are also seven points behind the leaders but they are third as the Paris club have the better goal difference.
PSG made a good start against Cannes, going ahead with striker Cyrille Pouget's first league goal for the club in the 12th minute.
But midfielder Laurent Charvet scored a shock equaliser for the visitors five minutes into the second half and the Paris club had to settle for a draw.
"We took only two points at home from the last three matches and that's obviously not satisfying," Ricardo said. "But I liked the spirit of the team today (Saturday), the way they never gave up."
Midfielder Benoit Cauet said he thought PSG had played slightly better than in their previous matches.
"A few weeks ago, in the same situation, we probably would have lost the match," he said. "After they scored the equaliser we kept trying. We'll be luckier next time."
Not only did PSG fail to win but they also lost a key player in central defender Alain Roche, who will be out of action for several weeks.
Roche, who only recently came back after a two-month injury break, fell in the 38th minute and hurt the right knee he had been nursing.
"I don't know how bad it is but I can't walk, so it doesn't look too good," he said.

PSG, European Cup Winners' Cup holders, had said their main goal this season would be to take the league title from Auxerre. They were regarded as clear favourites but their troubles began last September when international goalkeeper Bernard Lama suffered a nasty knee injury.
He came back in late October but appeared far from his best form as Paris lost 5-3 at Nantes, were crushed 6-1 at home by Juventus in the European Super Cup and then, critically, lost 2-0 to Monaco.
Lama is not the only one to blame for PSG's poor results as Brazilian stars Leonardo and Rai, who were brilliant early in the season, have failed to shine of late.
"What we need now is a win," said Pouget, who joined during the winter break. "A victory would bring back confidence."
Paris will probably think of a banner held by their fans on Saturday when they face Juventus in the Super Cup return match on Wednesday.
